newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi insurance premium growth slows in '95 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi insurance premium growth slows in '95 - paper.

text.p: Insurance premium growth in Saudi Arabia slowed to 5.5 percent in 1995 from record growth of up to 18 percent in the early 1990s, according to a study published on Thursday in the local Arab News paper.

The study by the National Company for Cooperative Insurance (NCCI) -- which groups most of the insurance companies in Saudi Arabia -- said the gross written premiums under various classes rose to 2.57 billion riyals ($685 million) in 1995 from 2.43 billion riyals in 1994.
The survey showed the highest growth rates were registered in engineering and medical insurance, while marine and car insurance premiums witnessed moderate growth rates.
It said the Saudi insurance industry employed 2,352 people last year.
